column1: # Every corpus case where CPython's json and node's JSON.parse disagree.
# Columns: name, cpython, node, why. Lines beginning with # are comments.
# Produced by:  python3 cases.py | tee /tmp/corpus.tsv | python3 classify.py
#               python3 classify.py < /tmp/corpus.tsv ; node classify.js < /tmp/corpus.tsv
# Run on 2026-07-30 with CPython 3.14.6 and node v22.23.1 (V8), 222 cases,
# 5 disagreements. Rerun after either tool is upgraded: this file is a
# measurement, not a specification.
# The map is smaller than the reputation of the problem suggests, and the reason
# is worth writing down: the two remaining classes are the only ones where a
# mainstream parser still reads bytes as a document that another mainstream
# parser refuses outright. Every other divergence in the corpus is a divergence
# between one of them and *us*, which lives in EXPECTATIONS.tsv, or it is a
# divergence in the value returned rather than in the verdict, which lives in
# values.py and floats.py.
# STACK-DEPENDENT CASES ARE EXCLUDED FROM THE PINNED SET, and one of them is why.
# i_structure_nested_100000_deep: on this laptop CPython and node BOTH accept it; on
# a GitHub ubuntu-latest runner they DISAGREE. Neither is wrong. A recursive descent
# parser's verdict on a hundred-thousand-deep document is decided by how much stack
# the process was given, so a row for it would pin the machine rather than the
# parser, and tests/oracle.rs skips it in the equality and asserts instead the thing
# that holds everywhere: we refuse it as a Limit, never as a syntax error.
# Measured 2026-07-30, laptop CPython 3.14.6 / node v22.23.1 both accept; the first
# public CI run on 91f1733 measured a disagreement and failed the build, which is
# how this note came to exist.
# One caveat stated plainly, because it flatters the agreement number: the
# sixteen invalid-UTF-8 cases agree partly by construction. classify.js checks
# the bytes round-trip through Buffer.toString before JSON.parse sees them,
# because node's decoder substitutes U+FFFD instead of failing. Without that
# check node would accept most of them as documents full of replacement
# characters and the disagreement count would be sixteen higher.
n_number_infinity
column4: CPython's scanner has three non-standard literals built in, and Infinity is one of them; JSON has none and V8 refuses it, which makes CPython the outlier here rather than node.

column1: n_number_negative_infinity
column4: Same non-standard literal with a sign, handled as a special case in CPython's scanner before the number grammar is consulted at all.

column1: n_number_nan
column4: CPython returns float('nan'); the value then compares unequal to itself, so a record carrying it can never be matched against a copy of itself.

column1: n_number_infinity_as_object_value
column4: The same three literals are accepted anywhere a value belongs, not only at the top level, so a single member is enough to make a document unportable.

column1: i_number_5000_digit_integer
column4: CPython refuses to convert an integer literal of more than 4300 digits (the CVE-2020-10735 mitigation, on by default since 3.11) and raises ValueError, not JSONDecodeError; node reads the same digits as a double and hands back Infinity, so the value that reaches the caller is not in the document.
